title: E212: Add a lot of missing MCC/MNC codes

notes.body:
So where do those PLMN codes come from? This dissector is filled with the ITU-T E.212 list and you have an indication at the beginning of the file giving the recommendation used. How will we keep track of the changes done here?
Note that your indentation does not match the one used in the file.
Forget the comment regarding the indentation: this was a browser bug on my side that does not happen anymore.
I mostly used http://www.mcc-mnc.com that was referenced in the comments in the code.  I updated a few from wikipedia (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mobile_Network_Codes_in_ITU_region_4xx_(Asia))

The www.mcc-mnc.com website does not provide any information regarding its last update, and the copyright info (hopefully wrong) indicates 2011-2013. I'm not sure whether we should consider this source as being a reference or not.

The best would be to use the GSMA TS.25 list (which allows you to extract the information much more easily and automate the update) but as far as I know its access requires being a member. I know ITU-T list seems to be lagging behind but as it is updated twice a month, it gives me the feeling that operators are not declaring their PLMN to this group. And TS.25 indicates that E.212 the authoritative reference, as seen in https://www.gsma.com/newsroom/wp-content/uploads//TS.25-v5.0.pdf

We have been suffering from this kind of issues since years, but using another reference than ITU-T means that this is no more the E.212 list (for the good and the bad).
@JaapKeuter I'm not sure whether the www.mcc-mnc.com reference is still applicable following your last update or not. Could you clarify?

https://github.com/P1sec/MCC_MNC also contains some interesting info (and indicates that www.mcc-mnc.com cannot be blindly trusted). It seems like they have automated the ITU-T E.212 bulletin extraction. This is something we could look at.

  • 3ba4568f - E212: Add comment referencing wikipedia
[Compare with previous version](/wireshark/wireshark/-/merge_requests/629/diffs?diff_id=118820650&start_sha=ccd89ae5878032faa654aefd43d98805a2dd46a3)

@pquantin The site mcc-mnc.com was used only to amend the information retrieved from the ITU-T bulletins, in places where the previous source file had several entries while the ITU-T bulletins did not provide this information. 
All this is explicitly documented in the start of the source file.
```
 * Annex to ITU Operational Bulletin
 * No. 1162 - 15.XII.2018
 *
 * With Amendment No. 1 (T-SP-OB 1164 - 15.I.2019) up to and
 * including Amendment No. 34 (T-SP-OB 1198 - 15.VI.2020)
 *
 * COMPLEMENT TO ITU-T RECOMMENDATION E.212 (09/2016)
 * WITH Rec. ITU-T E.212 (2016)/Amd.2
 *
 * Find the bulletins here: http://www.itu.int/pub/T-SP-OB
 *
 * Amended with information from http://www.mcc-mnc.com
 * - Chinese PLMN codes
 * - Iranian PLMN codes
```

Hi @JaapKeuter ,
I know this was used before, my question was more whether you used www.mcc-mnc.com for the major update you did a few weeks back. I now see that you touched those lines so I get my answer. I'm not fully confident in the information found on this website (as we do not know when it was last updated).

Hi @pquantin, indeed the authoritative source of information was the ITU-T bulletins. Only where a significant gap existed in the ITU-T listing this secondary source was considered, of which the accuracy cannot be ascertained. This was also partly done to prevent an influx of MRs like this when dropping these entries.

>We have been suffering from this kind of issues since years

Because and I quote "unfortunately, the official list is often incomplete as national MNC authorities do not forward changes to the ITU in a timely manner." From wikipedia.
